scenes.title: Your skin barrier is a brick wall.
scenes.say: Your skin barrier is basically a brick wall.

scenes.title: Cells are the bricks. Lipids are the mortar.
scenes.say: The bricks are skin cells. The mortar between them is lipids, mostly ceramides.

scenes.title: Too much scrubbing cracks the mortar.
scenes.say: Exfoliate too often, and the mortar starts to crack.

scenes.title: Water escapes. Irritants get in.
scenes.say: Water escapes, irritants get in. That's the redness and the tight feeling.

scenes.title: Fix it with ceramides. Pause the acids.
scenes.say: To fix it, use a ceramide cream and pause the acids for a week.

scenes.title: Save this before your next exfoliation.
scenes.say: Save this before your next exfoliation.

kobi.caption:
Your skin barrier is a brick wall 🧱
Skin cells are the bricks, lipids are the mortar. Over-exfoliate and the mortar cracks: water escapes, irritants get in. Ceramides and a break from acids fix it.
Save this before your next exfoliation.

scenes.title: SPF is only half the story.
scenes.say: SPF is only half the story.

scenes.title: UVB burns the surface.
scenes.say: U V B rays hit the top layer of your skin. That's sunburn, and that's what SPF measures.

scenes.title: UVA goes deeper and ages skin.
scenes.say: U V A rays go deeper, down to the collagen. That's wrinkles and dark spots. And they pass through windows.

scenes.title: PA++++ = top UVA protection.
scenes.say: In Korea, the P A rating measures U V A. Four plus signs is the highest.

scenes.title: Look for SPF50+ PA++++. Save this.
scenes.say: So look for S P F fifty plus, P A four plus. Save this.

kobi.caption:
SPF is only half the story ☀️
SPF measures UVB, the burning rays. UVA goes deeper, ages your skin and passes through windows. In Korea the PA rating covers it: PA++++ is the top grade.
Save this and check your sunscreen.

scenes.title: Why Koreans wash their face twice.
scenes.say: Why do Koreans wash their face twice?

scenes.title: Sunscreen and makeup are oil-based.
scenes.say: Sunscreen, makeup and sebum are oil based. Water alone just slides off them.

scenes.title: Oil dissolves oil.
scenes.say: An oil cleanser grabs them, because oil dissolves oil.

scenes.title: Then a gentle foam.
scenes.say: Then a gentle foam cleanser washes away what's left.

scenes.title: Do it at night. Save this.
scenes.say: Do it at night, not in the morning. Save this.

kobi.caption:
Why Koreans wash their face twice 🫧
Sunscreen, makeup and sebum are oil-based, so water slides off. An oil cleanser dissolves them, then a gentle foam removes the rest. Night only.
Save this for tonight.

scenes.title: Why Seoul has almost no trash cans.
scenes.say: Ever noticed Seoul has almost no trash cans on the street?

scenes.title: 1995: you pay for your trash.
scenes.say: In 1995, Korea started charging for household trash. You have to buy special bags for it.

scenes.title: So people used street bins instead.
scenes.say: So some people dumped their home trash in public bins instead. And many cities took the bins away.

scenes.title: Today: carry it, sort it.
scenes.say: Today, locals carry their trash and sort it. Try convenience stores and metro stations.

scenes.title: Now you know. Send this to your travel buddy.
scenes.say: Now you know. Send this to your travel buddy.

dari.caption:
Why Seoul has almost no trash cans 🗑️
In 1995 Korea started charging for household trash with special bags. Some people dumped it in street bins instead, so many bins disappeared. Today you carry it and sort it.
Send this to your travel buddy.
